title: Frame-dependent coherence of Gaussian quantum states
abstract: A Hilbert space is usually described using an orthonormal basis, but a more general description can be defined using a tight frame. In the case of continuous-variable Gaussian states, the coherence is usually described using the Hermite-Gauss basis. We present an alternative description using the tight frame of all canonical coherent states. The description of Gaussian states in terms of coherent states is simpler than in terms of Hermite-Gauss basis, and this allows us to obtain an explicit formula describing the frame-dependent coherence of a mixed Gaussian state as a function of the determinant and the trace of covariance matrix. For each mixed Gaussian state, we construct a sequence of discrete-variable quantum states rapidly convergent to it (as concern the purity and coherence) when the dimension of Hilbert space becomes large enough (15 or more). In the discrete case, the coherence is measured with respect to the tight frame of all discrete coherent states.
summary: This paper introduces a frame-dependent measure of coherence for Gaussian quantum states, moving beyond traditional basis-dependent definitions. It derives an explicit formula for this coherence using the covariance matrix for continuous variables and establishes a rigorous connection to the discrete variable case. This provides a more robust and general tool for quantifying quantum coherence in Gaussian systems.
main_problem: The paper develops an alternative method to quantify quantum state coherence for Gaussian states by utilizing a 'tight frame' description instead of standard orthonormal bases or the Hermite-Gauss basis.
main_result: An explicit, closed-form formula for the frame-dependent coherence of a mixed Gaussian state is derived, expressed simply in terms of the determinant and trace of the state's covariance matrix.
method: The authors generalize the $\ell_1$-norm of coherence to tight frames, deriving specific formulas for both continuous-variable (CV) and discrete-variable (DV) Gaussian states, and analyzing the convergence between the two descriptions.
model_or_system: The focus is on single-mode, pure or mixed, Gaussian quantum states, which are characterized mathematically by their covariance matrix ($\sigma$) in the continuous case, and by discrete Wigner functions in the discrete case.
key_observables: Frame-dependent coherence ($	ext{CF}(ho)$), Purity ($	ext{tr} ho^2$), Covariance matrix ($\sigma$).
important_parameters: The dimension of the Hilbert space ($d$), the determinant ($\det \sigma$), and the trace ($	ext{tr} \sigma$) of the covariance matrix.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the mathematical framework of tight frames and the assumption that the discrete system converges to the continuous limit as the dimension increases.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of frame-dependent coherence, then derives the general formula for CVGS using the covariance matrix, and finally extends this analysis to DVGS, demonstrating the convergence between the two descriptions.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, basis-independent tool (frame-dependent coherence) to characterize quantum states, which is crucial for understanding how coherence measures behave when the underlying mathematical description of the state space is generalized beyond standard orthonormal bases.
